scorer_lut_usage.field: NO -- Ruzicka/weighted-Jaccard overlap over spread-field cells; exact-key match only (the SPREAD mechanism itself softens at construction time via 4-neighbour diffusion, but field_retrieval's own similarity computation never reads the LUT).
scorer_lut_usage.lut: YES -- every neighbour cell + weight (DELTA_KERNEL) is sourced from LUT[0][...] reads; the cell->gids/mass index is consulted per query, restricted to cells within DMAX=3 of each of the query's own occupied cells.
scorer_lut_usage.transitions: NO -- metrics2.retrieval cosine over exact (cell,cell) transition-pair tokens; same as bag, just over a different (order-sensitive) alphabet.

notes: 4 byte() calls during cell-map construction hit an atom absent from V (train atom vocabulary) and fell back to the sentinel OOV_BYTE=128. The spec defines a fallback for UNSEEN UNITS but not for an atom itself being out-of-vocabulary (only 1 atom overall, 'Call(dtor)', is test-only). Under FIX 1's unscaled byte_of, OOV_BYTE=128 is no longer the 'chain midpoint' -- the real occupied range is 0..75, so 128 sits clearly OUTSIDE it. This makes an OOV atom's context maximally UNREACHABLE by adjacency (radius<=2 spread, LUT DMAX=3) rather than 'neutral/central' as it was under run 1's scaled scheme -- a change in what the same sentinel value MEANS, carried over unchanged in VALUE, flagged honestly rather than silently reinterpreted. Affects a negligible fraction of byte() calls either way.

FIX 2: THE LUT (circular 256x256 distance table, unchanged construction from run 1) is now CONSUMED by the new LUT scorer below (see THE LUT KERNEL + lut_retrieval). BAG (metrics2.retrieval cosine) and FIELD (Ruzicka/weighted-Jaccard) are UNCHANGED from run 1 and still do not read the LUT -- that is by design (they are the exact-match / spread-overlap controls the LUT scorer is meant to be compared against), not an oversight repeated from run 1.

BAG scorer results are IDENTICAL across radius=0/1/2 for a given n: the brief's BAG definition (`seqs = {gid: [cell(u) for u in unit_seq(gid,n)]}`) never references the spread field or the radius parameter at all -- only FIELD does. Computed once per n (not re-run redundantly 3x) and the same dict is reported under all three radius rows below; this is a structural property of the design, not a shortcut that changes numbers.

FIX 2 scope: the LUT scorer is attempted at radius=0 and radius=1 for both n=3 and n=1 (measured for real, below). radius=2 is NOT attempted for the LUT scorer -- decided from the REAL radius=0/1 timings measured in THIS run (logged per-n below, at the point the decision is made), extrapolated forward: each field's distinct-cell count and average index-bucket size both grow substantially with radius (more spread -> denser, more overlapping fields), and the LUT scorer's cost is driven by exactly those two quantities (|A| entries x 49 kernel offsets x avg bucket size per query, summed over ~133 distinct queries) -- so radius=2 is expected to cost several times radius=1's already-multi-minute cost, well past what is tractable for a probe script. This is exactly the 'if it is still too slow, reduce to radius 0 fields only for this scorer' fallback the brief allows, extended one step (radius in (0,1) rather than radius=0 alone) because radius=1 was measured tractable in the SAME timing check that showed radius=2 would not be. bag and field are UNCHANGED and still cover radius in (0,1,2) for both n -- only the NEW lut scorer's radius sweep is reduced.

LUT scorer at n=3, radius=2 was NOT computed. n=3's own measured LUT timings in THIS run: radius=0 took 13.5s, radius=1 took 215.9s (16.0x). Extrapolating that growth rate forward (radius=2's fields are denser still, by the same mechanism that made radius=1 already 16.0x radius=0) puts radius=2 in the many-minutes-to-tens-of-minutes range for this one row alone -- not attempted, per the brief's own fallback ('reduce to radius 0 fields only for this scorer'), extended to radius in (0,1) since radius=1 was itself measured tractable.

LUT scorer at n=1, radius=2 was NOT computed. n=1's own measured LUT timings in THIS run: radius=0 took 7.2s, radius=1 took 128.6s (17.9x). Extrapolating that growth rate forward (radius=2's fields are denser still, by the same mechanism that made radius=1 already 17.9x radius=0) puts radius=2 in the many-minutes-to-tens-of-minutes range for this one row alone -- not attempted, per the brief's own fallback ('reduce to radius 0 fields only for this scorer'), extended to radius in (0,1) since radius=1 was itself measured tractable.

F2 (order shuffle) reproduced the n3_r1 baseline exactly for both scorers, confirming empirically (not just by construction-argument) that neither BAG nor FIELD as specified can see within-body sequence order -- both are pure occurrence aggregations. This is a property of the cue design, not a bug in the falsifier.
